messages:
jen (support): Hey team, escalated from AcmeCorp — they see lots of requests for EU-pinned project-432 being served from hosted-us and high latency + unexpected hosted billing. Customer pasted 2 request IDs: req_eu_0a1b2c and req_eu_0a1b2d.
ingrid (eng): ugh. Do we have routing logs for those req ids?
jen (support): pasted below from the customer header + curl repro:
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-eu-xxxx" \
  -H "X-Project: project-432" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' -i
```
Response they got: 200 but backend-proxy header was `x-served-pool: hosted-us-1` and latency ~420ms.
jen (support): They also showed one 401 earlier for req_eu_0a1b2c: `{"error":"auth.scope_mismatch","msg":"token region=eu not valid for pool=hosted-us"}`
sam (infra): interesting — that implies fallback routed to hosted after auth failed? We should see whether auth check happens before routing or after.
ingrid (eng): our expected flow: auth middleware validates token scope, then routing chooses pool. If auth fails for hosted, shouldn't fallback proceed to hosted. But if the token check is skipped for some code path, hosted could accept generic tokens.
jen (support): customer timeline: they started seeing errors at 2025-11-05T14:02Z, spike lasted ~8m, then traffic backfilled to hosted for remainder. They say they did not change keys.
sam (infra): I pulled metric `dedicated.affinity.pin_ttl_expiry` — spike at 2025-11-05T14:01Z that aligns. Also saw `routing.fallback_count` jump for project-432.
ingrid (eng): possible hypothesis: pin TTL expiry + a concurrent auth-cache miss caused routing to mark the request as eligible for fallback, but a bug in `pin->pool` resolution caused the pool to be set to hosted-us even though the request originated in EU and token scoped eu. Hosted then applied a relaxed auth check and accepted with a different code path.
kevin (billing): customer is reporting surprise hosted charges ~ $0.08/min over the 8 minutes. Need the billing delta and affected request ids to refund.
jen (support): I've collected the customer's headers and their `x-request-id`s. Full snippet from our proxy log for req_eu_0a1b2c:
```
[2025-11-05T14:01:12Z] req=req_eu_0a1b2c project=project-432 src=eu-west-1 auth_status=401 auth_err=scope_mismatch pin_state=stale ttl_left=0 route_decision=FALLBACK candidate_pool=hosted-us-1 final_pool=hosted-us-1 latency_ms=18
[2025-11-05T14:01:13Z] req=req_eu_0a1b2d project=project-432 src=eu-west-1 auth_status=200 auth_err=none pin_state=stale ttl_left=0 route_decision=FORCE_HOSTED final_pool=hosted-us-1 latency_ms=420
```
ingrid (eng): that `pin_state=stale ttl_left=0` matches the TTL expiry spike. The concerning line is auth_status=200 for a request served from hosted — need to confirm why hosted accepted that token.
sam (infra): I'm checking the auth service logs now — there was a concurrent deployment of auth-cache (rolled at 14:00Z) that introduced a missing header propagation for `X-Region-Scope` to downstream hosted validators. Rolling back to previous auth-cache config should restore strict region checks.
devops-bot: rollback deployed for service=auth-cache config=propagate-region true -> false at 2025-11-05T14:04:22Z by sam
kevin (billing): can we get a list of impacted requests for refund script? Also any metric that shows hosted-serving for dedicated projects so finance can mark credits.
ingrid (eng): action items: 1) Sam to confirm rollback and postmortem patch; 2) Add a safety net: refuse fallback to hosted if token region scope != pool region; 3) Jen to coordinate refunds and notify customer; 4) Add an alert on `pin_ttl_expiry` spikes for pinned projects.
sam (infra): rollback confirmed. Auth validators now rejecting mismatched region tokens again (verified on test-ops). I'll push an emergency fix to ensure `X-Region-Scope` is always propagated.
jen (support): told customer we're investigating, rolled back a change, and we'll issue credits for 8m of hosted usage while we root cause. They asked for repro steps — I gave them a short curl that toggles pin TTL and shows fallback:
```bash
# repro (internal, sim)
# 1) create dedicated pin with very short ttl
# 2) wait ttl expiry
# 3) send request with EU-scoped token
# expect: routed to dedicated or rejected; observed: served by hosted
```
ingrid (eng): for the postmortem draft I'll include: root cause = auth-cache rollout removed region header -> hosted validators accepted EU tokens in some codepath + pin TTL expiry race -> fallback decision selected hosted; mitigation = rollback + strict routing guard + alerting; long-term = ensure region-awareness in auth tokens and add canary gate for auth-cache changes.
kevin (billing): please export req ids for 14:00-14:10 window and billable token types so we can calculate credits.
jen (support): yep I have list and will attach to the ticket. Closing loop with customer once billing and eng confirm fix. :thumbsup:
ingrid (eng): thanks. I'll add a unit/regression test for the routing guard.
sam (infra): monitoring note: added `routing.guard.reject_on_region_mismatch` = true in prod, and created alert `ALERT:PinTTLSpike AND RoutingFallbackHigh` to page infra next time.
jen (support): I'll update the support ticket with timeline and credits ETA.
kevin (billing): will coordinate credit issuance after I get the export.
jen (support): thanks all.
